evidence.reference_title: Metabolic differentiation of early Lyme disease from southern tick-associated rash illness (STARI).
evidence.snippet: STARI, is associated with a bite from the lone star tick (Amblyomma americanum), and in addition to the development of an EM-like skin lesion, individuals with STARI can present with mild systemic symptoms (including muscle and joint pains, fatigue, fever, chills, and headache) that are similar to those occurring in patients with Lyme disease.

evidence.reference_title: Prospective clinical evaluation of patients from Missouri and New York with erythema migrans-like skin lesions.
evidence.snippet: EM-like lesions in Missouri cases were smaller in size than those in New York cases (8.3+/-2.2 cm and 16.4+/-11.5 cm, respectively; P<.001), more circular in shape (P=.004), and more likely to have central clearing (76.2% and 21.6%, respectively; P<.001).

nodes.description: At the Amblyomma americanum bite site, localized cutaneous vascular dilation and dermal inflammation generate a single, circular, expanding annular erythematous lesion with frequent central clearing, arising more rapidly after tick attachment and remaining smaller and less likely to disseminate than early Lyme erythema migrans.

evidence.reference_title: Prospective clinical evaluation of patients from Missouri and New York with erythema migrans-like skin lesions.
evidence.snippet: EM-like lesions in Missouri cases were smaller in size than those in New York cases (8.3+/-2.2 cm and 16.4+/-11.5 cm, respectively; P<.001), more circular in shape (P=.004), and more likely to have central clearing (76.2% and 21.6%, respectively; P<.001).

nodes.description: Bite of the lone star tick (Amblyomma americanum) is the defining antecedent arthropod exposure preceding the cutaneous lesion and mild systemic symptoms of STARI, although whether the bite transmits an uncharacterized infectious agent or delivers bioactive tick salivary factors remains unresolved.

evidence.reference_title: Prospective clinical evaluation of patients from Missouri and New York with erythema migrans-like skin lesions.
evidence.snippet: Case patients from Missouri were more likely to recall a tick bite than were case patients from New York (85.7% and 19.8%, respectively; P<.001), and the time period from tick bite to onset of the skin lesion was shorter among Missouri case patients (6.1+/-4.2 days and 10.4+/-6.1 days, respectively; P=.011).

nodes.description: Following an Amblyomma americanum bite, patients develop an acute cutaneous and mild systemic syndrome without a confirmed bacterial pathogen: skin biopsy culture, targeted Borrelia PCR, rickettsial serology, and contemporary 16S ribosomal RNA sequencing have repeatedly failed to identify Borrelia burgdorferi, Borrelia lonestari, or another causative bacterium.

evidence.reference_title: Microbiologic evaluation of patients from Missouri with erythema migrans.
evidence.snippet: Neither B. lonestari nor B. burgdorferi is likely to be the cause of EM-like skin lesions in patients from the Cape Girardeau area of Missouri. The etiology of this condition remains unknown.

evidence.reference_title: Epidemiologic and clinical characteristics and outcomes of patients diagnosed with Southern Tick Associated Rash Illness (STARI) - 2018-2019.
evidence.snippet: Using 16S sequencing, no known bacterial pathogen was detected. Although an etiologic agent remains unknown, these results do provide updated information on rash color, shape, duration, and treatment outcomes.

nodes.description: Patient-serum metabolomics identifies a systemic metabolic state in STARI that differs significantly from early Lyme disease, centered on altered N-acyl ethanolamine and primary fatty acid amide lipid-mediator signaling accompanying mild constitutional and musculoskeletal symptoms in a subset of patients.

evidence.reference_title: Metabolic differentiation of early Lyme disease from southern tick-associated rash illness (STARI).
evidence.snippet: Additionally, the metabolic biosignature revealed that N-acyl ethanolamine (NAE) and primary fatty acid amide (PFAM) metabolism differed significantly between these two diseases.

evidence.reference_title: Metabolic differentiation of early Lyme disease from southern tick-associated rash illness (STARI).
evidence.snippet: These findings revealed metabolic dissimilarity between early Lyme disease and STARI, and provide a powerful and new approach to inform patient management by objectively distinguishing early Lyme disease from an illness with nearly identical symptoms.
